answer: Honeypots split workers from clones cheaply. The ledger plants one fake job in every fifty, its spec self-contradicting. Each agent posts a 500 POA bond; finishing a planted job is a false signal that slashes the bond a quarter. Three hits and the identity is a relic, barred 180 epochs. Each trap carries its own pigment, a one-time nonce a botnet cannot share across copies. A farm of 1,000 clones eats 20 traps before its first payout: 10,000 bonds burned before it earns one credit. Like dead lures beside live worms, the copies strike first, and the line gives up nothing.
